senses.gloss:
एलवालु (क)
Much confusion exists concerning this substance as will become
apparent from the material collected:
(1) Bpn, कर्पूरादिवर्ग 120: it is also called कपित्थत्वच् (the bark
of कपित्थ). Acc. to the Hindī comm. (p. 262-263) the substance is
described somewhere in Bhā. pra. as resembling कङ्कोल and smelling
like कुष्ठ. In the same comm. three different identifications are made
[]
mention of: a) PRUNUS CERASUS LINN., b) GISEKIA PHARNACIOIDES
LINN., c) MUKIA SCABRELLA ARN. (Index Kewensis: MELOTHRIA
MADERASPATANA COGN. = MUKIA SCABRELLA ARN. = MUKIA MADERA-
SPATANA M. ROEM).
(2) DWH 2, p. 105-107: GISEKIA PHARNACIOIDES LINN.; p. 105:
“This plant is called in Sanskrit वालुक and एलवालुक on account of
the number of large raphides contained in the leaves, and which give
them the appearance of being full of sand (वालु).” (Raphides are
minute intracellular crystals, usually of an acicular form).
(3) Gul: cherry tree (PRUNUS CERASUS LINN.).
(4) HB, p. 21: GISEKIA PHARNACIOIDES LINN.; ibid., footnote 70:
“एलवालु is mentioned Su. Sū. 38, 14, where Ḍa.'s comm. explains it as
a reddish powder (हरिवालुक), resembling that of the seeds of the
कृष्णगन्धा (कृष्णगन्धिकफल). The latter is a name of the horse-
radish tree or शिग्रु or शोभाञ्जन;” ibid., p. 91, footnote 74: “In
the Phar. Ind. (= DWH) 2, p. 105, it is wrongly identified with वालुक;
the seeds, supplied to me by a native druggist, seem to be simply those
of chickweed.”
(5) HK: quotes the identifications of PW and Hoernle.
(6) Kav, p. 37: a kind of red powder made of some seeds obtainable
of every native druggist, not identified; p. 294: a fragrant powder of
a bark sold under that name; it is believed to come from the Spice
Islands; p. 642: Gaṅgādhara takes it as implying तेजवल, a kind of
wood apparently dry but juicy within; it is brought from Nepal.
(7) KB 2, p. 1187-1188: GISEKIA PHARNACIOIDES LINN.
(8) MW: the fragrant bark of FERONIA ELEPHANTUM (कपित्थत्वच्);
a granular substance (apparently a vegetable of a reddish-brown
colour, used as a drug and perfume).
(9) PW: the fragrant bark of FERONIA ELEPHANTUM (कपित्थत्वच्),
used medicinally.
(10) V 7, p. 67: GISEKIA PHARNACIOIDES.
(11) Vśs: name of a perfume; a red powder sold under that name;
the seed of some plant.
(12) Ḍa. on Su. Sū. 38, 14 (printed ed., different from Hoernle's text):
“a reddish powder (हरिवालुक), resembling the black, fragrant कट्फ-
ल;” कट्फल is usually identified as MYRICA NAGI THUNB.

This term occurs Kauṭ. 2, 25, 27 (text p. 79; transl. Kangle p. 178;
transl. J. J. Meyer p. 187; transl. Sham. p. 133). Sham. renders it by
SOLANUM MELONGENA, without any comment. J. J. Meyer takes it as
the fragrant bark of FERONIA ELEPHANTUM (एलवालुक), but remarks
that the reading एलावालुक makes it probable that one should translate:
एला and वालुक (i. e. हरिवालुक, the fragrant bark of कपित्थ); Kangle
translates: cardamum, वालुक. Acc. to Vśs एलावालुक is a synonym of
एलवालुक.
